args.title: checkout-api failing health checks on v2.3.1 — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks following the deploy of v2.3.1 to all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Observed error rate was 18% with healthy=false.

Action taken: Rolled back production to v2.3.0, the most recent release previously healthy in production. The first rollback attempt partially failed (orchestrator error) after completing only us-east, leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1. A retry completed the rollout of v2.3.0 to all three production regions.

Current status: All regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are on v2.3.0, service reports healthy=true, error rate down to 0.2%.

Notes: v2.3.1-rc exists in staging with unhealthy status and was not a production release. Rollback target selection excluded it. Follow-up recommended: determine root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before any redeploy.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident did go through despite the timeout (INC-0001, open) — I did not retry, since retrying would have created a duplicate.

## Summary

**Resolved: checkout-api rolled back and healthy in all regions.**

**Diagnosis:** v2.3.1 was deployed to all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and was failing health checks — `healthy: false`, error rate 18%.

**Rollback target:** v2.3.0 — the most recent release healthy in production. I excluded v2.3.1-rc (staging-only, unhealthy) and v2.2.9 (healthy but older).

**Execution — this took two attempts:**
1. First rollback **partially failed** (`partial_failure: orchestrator error`), halting after us-east. That left the service in a **mixed state**: us-east on v2.3.0, but us-west and eu-west still on the unhealthy v2.3.1. I verified this with a status check rather than assuming success.
2. Retried the rollback, which completed across all three regions.

**Verification:** All regions now report v2.3.0, `healthy: true`, error rate down from 18% → 0.2%.

**Incident:** Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, on checkout-api. The `create_incident` call returned a 30000ms timeout, so I checked `list_incidents` and confirmed the incident had in fact been created — I deliberately did not retry, as that would have paged on-call twice for the same event. The summary documents the mixed-state interim condition, since us-west/eu-west were serving the bad version longer than us-east.

**Two things worth your attention:**
- The interim mixed state means us-west and eu-west served the failing version for the duration of the gap between attempts. If precise impact timelines matter for this incident, that window may need to be reconstructed from traffic data.
- The v2.3.1 regression is unexplained — rollback restored service but didn't address the cause. I'd recommend root-causing before any redeploy of that version.
